records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 alloy (multi-principal-element alloy). Test conditions: Room temperature tensile tests at strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. item.intervention: Tested at elevated temperatures of 600°C and 700°C
item.processing: High-temperature tensile tests conducted on Gleeble 3500 system at strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ in argon atmosphere (0.05 MPa)

the proof stress, fracture stress and elongation were 95 MPa, 806 MPa, 33.7%, and 108 MPa, 538 MPa, 22.9%, respectively

item.intervention: Cold rolled with a thick reduction of 8%

item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile tests at strain rate 2 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹

item.intervention: Characterized phase constitution via XRD and DSC
item.processing: XRD using Shimadzu XRD-6000 with Cu target (20°–100° 2θ, 4°/min); DSC using Netzsch STA 449 F3 (10 K/min heating/cooling)
item.structure_change: fcc/B2 dual-phase constitution; single melting event in DSC confirming eutectic composition
item.attributed_mechanism: Correlating the compositional information and the XRD result, the A regions shall correspond to the fcc phase while the B regions (including B II ) to the B2 phase
quotes: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the alloy is given in Fig. 3a , showing an fcc/B2 dual-phase constitution

The coupled grown two phases showed a clear compositional contrast

item.intervention: Investigated microstructure using SEM and EDS

item.processing: Preparation of ~2.5 kg ingot via conventional casting

item.intervention: Proposed design strategy using eutectic concept for HEAs
item.processing: Design based on pseudo-binary multi-component alloy system, varying concentration of one element systematically
item.property_change: Unprecedented combination of high fracture strength and high ductility
item.attributed_mechanism: To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept, i.e. to achieve a microstructure composed of alternating soft fcc and hard bcc phases
quotes: To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept
we proposed to design the eutectic alloys with a mixture of soft fcc and hard bcc phases, to achieve the balance of high fracture strength and high ductility
